title: Canonical terminal germ injective
statement: Let K be a field, Ks a separable closure, and Omega an algebraically closed extension containing Ks over K with the compatible scalar tower. Let T be terminal in the small etale site of Spec K, and x its geometric lift. Let E be an equivalence from abelian sheaves to discrete continuous integer Galois representations, with an additive natural stalk isomorphism i. No action-compatibility hypothesis is needed for injectivity. For every sheaf F, the map F(T) to E(F) given by the germ at x followed by i_F inverse is injective.

proof.text:
Equality of germs is witnessed on a common pointed etale neighbourhood.
Its structural map to Spec K is an etale surjection: its image is nonempty and
Spec K has one point. It therefore covers the terminal object. The separatedness
part of the sheaf condition makes restriction along this cover injective.
The two terminal sections are equal. Transport through the additive stalk
isomorphism preserves and reflects equality. In Lean, filtered-colimit preservation of the additive-group forgetful functor supplies the equality criterion. Terminality gives a retract of the identity etale object, so T has a singleton underlying space. Apply the singleton-cover separatedness criterion to the underlying sheaf of types.
